ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing types of evidence accepted for learning recognition evaluation.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionEvidenceCategory

Values.Description: Official documentation of a person’s assessment results.
Document verifying successful completion of structured training with an identifiable provider.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:CompletionRecord
dct:description: Applies to employer, community-based, military, or continuing education training.

Values.Description: Representation of a credential, digital or non-digital, attesting to a person’s achievements.
Recommendation for credit or competency value issued by an authoritative evaluating body, including amount, level, and conditions for specified learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:CreditRecommendation
dct:description: In the U.S., common sources include ACE credit recommendations.

Values.Description: Formal statement from an employer verifying duties, scope of work, and performance relevant to claimed learning.
Record confirming supervised practice, clinical hours, or comparable time-based experience.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:HoursVerification
dct:description: Common in clinical, practicum, apprenticeship, or licensure contexts.

Values.Description: Official role description with verification of incumbency and dates.
Official record of a person’s military education, training, occupations, and related evaluations.
Curated collection of artifacts evidencing learning typically aligned to defined outcomes.
Structured reflection connecting prior experience to defined competencies or outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:ReflectiveNarrative
dct:description: Often required in portfolio submissions. There may be a requirement for commentary or analysis in the narrative.

Values.Description: Structured record of experience and education accompanied by sufficient validation for evaluation.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:ResumeVerification
dct:description: Validation may include references, verification letters, or linked evidence.

Values.Description: Document that maps a person’s work artifacts or experiences to specified competencies, learning outcomes, or course requirements.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:SkillProfile
dct:description: Improves defensibility and transparency.

Values.Description: Document outlining objectives, content, requirements, schedule, and assessment for a specific course.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:Syllabus
dct:description: Supports content and outcome alignment.

Values.Description: Official academic record of a person’s achievements issued by the record holder.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:Transcript
dct:description: May be issued by the originating institution or a recognized clearinghouse.

Values.Description: Documentation of a person's on the job learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:WorkplaceLearningRecord
dct:description: Includes Apprentice Logbooks and similar.

Values.Description: Substantive work product demonstrating applied knowledge aligned to defined outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:WorkProduct
dct:description: May include reports, designs, code, media, or presentations.

learningRecognitionEvidenceType.description: Type of prior learning evidence accepted for evaluation under the policy; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing methods used to evaluate and recognize learning.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionMethodCategory

Values.Description: An evaluation method that uses an authoritative body’s credit recommendation to determine credit awards.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:CreditRecommendationReview
dct:description: In the U.S., examples include American Council on Education (ACE) credit recommendations.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which structured, external non-academic training is reviewed to award credit or standing.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:ExternalTrainingEvaluation
dct:description: May be conducted by employer, third-party, vendor, or external credentialing organization.

Values.Description: A method in which learning is assessed by a course-specific exam created and administered by faculty.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:FacultyDevelopedExamination
dct:description: In the United States, examples include challenge exams.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which faculty subject-matter experts judge whether prior learning meets course outcomes.
An evaluation method that uses personalized approaches to assess learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:IndividualizedPriorLearningAssessment
dct:description: Examples include portfolio review, simulation, and interview.

Values.Description: A method in which institution-created assessments are used to determine credit for prior learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:InstitutionDevelopedAssessment
dct:description: Examples include challenge exams, projects, and labs.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which learning or credit earned from organizations in other countries is reviewed for recognition.
A method in which a learner-developed portfolio is assessed to evidence prior learning aligned to defined outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:PortfolioAssessment
dct:description: Examples include documentation, work products, and artifacts mapped to competencies or requirements.

Values.Description: A structured method used to evaluate an individual's prior learning and its applicability to requirements.
A method in which learning is assessed by an exam used to demonstrate subject mastery for placement or credit.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:ProficiencyExamination
dct:description: May be internal or external; use Standardized Examination when using recognized national/international exams.

Values.Description: A method in which learning is assessed by a recognized standardized exam administered by an authoritative body.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:StandardizedExamination
dct:description: In the United States, examples include AP, CLEP, DLPT.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which prior records are reviewed to determine applicability.
An evaluation method that provides a preliminary determination of transferability using supplied records before matriculation.

learningRecognitionMethodType.description: Type of method used to evaluate and recognize prior learning; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing outcomes of learning recognition.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionOutcomeCategory

Values.Description: An outcome in which standing toward a program or qualification is granted, which may or may not carry transcripted credit.
An outcome in which learning results in transcripted credit.
An outcome in which learning fulfills a credit requirement.
An outcome in which a prerequisite, admission, or other eligibility requirement is satisfied by recognized learning.
An outcome in which a requirement is waived.
An outcome in which an evaluation is completed but no recognition is granted.
An outcome in which a person is placed into a program, hired or promoted.
An outcome in which learning is acknowledged for placement, exemption, or eligibility without awarding credit.

learningRecognitionOutcomeType.description: Type of outcome governed or permitted by the policy; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing formal, non-formal, or informal contexts from which learning may be recognized for applicability toward requirements.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionSourceCategory

Values.Description: Learning completed in a registered apprenticeship program.
Learning acquired through supervised clinical or practicum experiences in applied professional settings aligned to program or licensure standards.
Learning completed through structured training delivered by a community-based organization.
Learning acquired through unpaid service activities performed for the benefit of a community or organization outside a formal curriculum or assessed program.
Learning completed through structured, non-degree continuing education coursework.
Learning acquired through extended, alternating work–study placements integrated with an academic program.
Learning completed in a course, a structured sequence of educational activities designed to develop prescribed competencies.
Learning completed in educational programs while an individual is incarcerated or in custody.
Learning recognized on the basis of a previously awarded academic degree.
Learning completed in college-level coursework taken concurrently with secondary enrollment.
Learning completed through formal training provided by an employer or workforce development program.
Learning demonstrated via a recognized examination administered by a national, international, or military body.
Learning acquired through direct, hands-on experience with guided reflection in real or simulated settings.

learningRecognitionSourceType.description: Type of context from which prior learning may be recognized; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing types of evidence accepted for learning recognition evaluation.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionEvidenceCategory

Values.Description: Official documentation of a person’s assessment results.
Document verifying successful completion of structured training with an identifiable provider.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:CompletionRecord
dct:description: Applies to employer, community-based, military, or continuing education training.

Values.Description: Representation of a credential, digital or non-digital, attesting to a person’s achievements.
Recommendation for credit or competency value issued by an authoritative evaluating body, including amount, level, and conditions for specified learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:CreditRecommendation
dct:description: In the U.S., common sources include ACE credit recommendations.

Values.Description: Formal statement from an employer verifying duties, scope of work, and performance relevant to claimed learning.
Record confirming supervised practice, clinical hours, or comparable time-based experience.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:HoursVerification
dct:description: Common in clinical, practicum, apprenticeship, or licensure contexts.

Values.Description: Official role description with verification of incumbency and dates.
Official record of a person’s military education, training, occupations, and related evaluations.
Curated collection of artifacts evidencing learning typically aligned to defined outcomes.
Structured reflection connecting prior experience to defined competencies or outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:ReflectiveNarrative
dct:description: Often required in portfolio submissions. There may be a requirement for commentary or analysis in the narrative.

Values.Description: Structured record of experience and education accompanied by sufficient validation for evaluation.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:ResumeVerification
dct:description: Validation may include references, verification letters, or linked evidence.

Values.Description: Document that maps a person’s work artifacts or experiences to specified competencies, learning outcomes, or course requirements.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:SkillProfile
dct:description: Improves defensibility and transparency.

Values.Description: Document outlining objectives, content, requirements, schedule, and assessment for a specific course.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:Syllabus
dct:description: Supports content and outcome alignment.

Values.Description: Official academic record of a person’s achievements issued by the record holder.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:Transcript
dct:description: May be issued by the originating institution or a recognized clearinghouse.

Values.Description: Documentation of a person's on the job learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:WorkplaceLearningRecord
dct:description: Includes Apprentice Logbooks and similar.

Values.Description: Substantive work product demonstrating applied knowledge aligned to defined outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrEvidence:WorkProduct
dct:description: May include reports, designs, code, media, or presentations.

learningRecognitionEvidenceType.description: Type of prior learning evidence accepted for evaluation under the policy; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing methods used to evaluate and recognize learning.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionMethodCategory

Values.Description: An evaluation method that uses an authoritative body’s credit recommendation to determine credit awards.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:CreditRecommendationReview
dct:description: In the U.S., examples include American Council on Education (ACE) credit recommendations.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which structured, external non-academic training is reviewed to award credit or standing.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:ExternalTrainingEvaluation
dct:description: May be conducted by employer, third-party, vendor, or external credentialing organization.

Values.Description: A method in which learning is assessed by a course-specific exam created and administered by faculty.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:FacultyDevelopedExamination
dct:description: In the United States, examples include challenge exams.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which faculty subject-matter experts judge whether prior learning meets course outcomes.
An evaluation method that uses personalized approaches to assess learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:IndividualizedPriorLearningAssessment
dct:description: Examples include portfolio review, simulation, and interview.

Values.Description: A method in which institution-created assessments are used to determine credit for prior learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:InstitutionDevelopedAssessment
dct:description: Examples include challenge exams, projects, and labs.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which learning or credit earned from organizations in other countries is reviewed for recognition.
A method in which a learner-developed portfolio is assessed to evidence prior learning aligned to defined outcomes.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:PortfolioAssessment
dct:description: Examples include documentation, work products, and artifacts mapped to competencies or requirements.

Values.Description: A structured method used to evaluate an individual's prior learning and its applicability to requirements.
A method in which learning is assessed by an exam used to demonstrate subject mastery for placement or credit.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:ProficiencyExamination
dct:description: May be internal or external; use Standardized Examination when using recognized national/international exams.

Values.Description: A method in which learning is assessed by a recognized standardized exam administered by an authoritative body.
Values.Notes:
concept: lrMethod:StandardizedExamination
dct:description: In the United States, examples include AP, CLEP, DLPT.

Values.Description: An evaluation method in which prior records are reviewed to determine applicability.
An evaluation method that provides a preliminary determination of transferability using supplied records before matriculation.

learningRecognitionMethodType.description: Type of method used to evaluate and recognize prior learning; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing outcomes of learning recognition.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionOutcomeCategory

Values.Description: An outcome in which standing toward a program or qualification is granted, which may or may not carry transcripted credit.
An outcome in which learning results in transcripted credit.
An outcome in which learning fulfills a credit requirement.
An outcome in which a prerequisite, admission, or other eligibility requirement is satisfied by recognized learning.
An outcome in which a requirement is waived.
An outcome in which an evaluation is completed but no recognition is granted.
An outcome in which a person is placed into a program, hired or promoted.
An outcome in which learning is acknowledged for placement, exemption, or eligibility without awarding credit.

learningRecognitionOutcomeType.description: Type of outcome governed or permitted by the policy; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

ValueSet.Description: Concepts describing formal, non-formal, or informal contexts from which learning may be recognized for applicability toward requirements.
ValueSet.Name: LearningRecognitionSourceCategory

Values.Description: Learning completed in a registered apprenticeship program.
Learning acquired through supervised clinical or practicum experiences in applied professional settings aligned to program or licensure standards.
Learning completed through structured training delivered by a community-based organization.
Learning acquired through unpaid service activities performed for the benefit of a community or organization outside a formal curriculum or assessed program.
Learning completed through structured, non-degree continuing education coursework.
Learning acquired through extended, alternating work–study placements integrated with an academic program.
Learning completed in a course, a structured sequence of educational activities designed to develop prescribed competencies.
Learning completed in educational programs while an individual is incarcerated or in custody.
Learning recognized on the basis of a previously awarded academic degree.
Learning completed in college-level coursework taken concurrently with secondary enrollment.
Learning completed through formal training provided by an employer or workforce development program.
Learning demonstrated via a recognized examination administered by a national, international, or military body.
Learning acquired through direct, hands-on experience with guided reflection in real or simulated settings.

learningRecognitionSourceType.description: Type of context from which prior learning may be recognized; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

Values.Description: Credit that is issued or accepted as being related to one or more academic years.

Values.Description: Credit that is issued or accepted as being related to one or more temporal hours.

Values.Description: Credit that is applicable to two different educational levels.

Credit that is issued or accepted for some type of requirement.
Credit that is issued or accepted for a secondary diploma.

concept: creditUnit:SecondaryDiplomaCredit
broader: creditUnit:TypeBasedCredit
dct:description: Includes credits earned while enrolled in a secondary diploma program that meet graduation requirements.

Values.Description: Credit that is issued or accepted at a semester level.
Credit with a unit of measurement based on time, either figuratively or literally.
Credit with a unit of measurement based on the type of credit.

ValueSet.Description: Types of levels in an academic or training progression expected of, or to be developed by, the typical person for the resource being described.
ValueSet.Name: AudienceLevel

Values.Description: Intended for those with significant experience or expertise where developmental expectations are staged for assessing knowledge, skills, or competencies beyond the novice and intermediate levels.
Intended for those completing college/university-level programs within their first one to two years (lower-division) of post-secondary education.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:AssociatesDegreeLevel
broader: audLevel:PostSecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 5 – Short-cycle tertiary education.

Values.Description: Intended for those completing college/university-level programs within approximately three to four years where course work and activities advance skills from a lower-division or generalist level to an upper-division level.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:BachelorsDegreeLevel
broader: audLevel:PostSecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 6 – Bachelor’s or equivalent level.

Values.Description: Intended for novices or those with limited experience.
Intended for those who have completed Bachelors and Masters degrees or their equivalent and who will be required to complete either independent research or a significant project or paper.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:DoctoralDegreeLevel
broader: audLevel:PostSecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 8 – Doctoral or equivalent level.

Values.Description: Intended for children before the start of primary education.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:EarlyChildhood
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 0 – Early childhood education.

Values.Description: Intended for those who enrolled in a degree program or other formal program above the baccalaureate level, such as a masters or doctoral degree program.
Intended for those with some experience, where knowledge, skills, and competency expectations are staged for development beyond novice-level and in preparation for a more advanced-level.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:IntermediateLevel
dct:description: An individual at this level has foundational competencies to function independently with occasional supervision.

Values.Description: Intended for those in the first half of an undergraduate level program.
Intended for those at the earlier stages of secondary education, building on primary education, typically with a more subject-oriented curriculum.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:LowerSecondary
broader: audLevel:SecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 2 – Lower secondary education.

Values.Description: Intended for those who have completed a Bachelor's Degree or equivalent.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:MastersDegreeLevel
broader: audLevel:PostSecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 7 – Master’s or equivalent level.

Values.Description: Intended for those who have completed secondary level school programs or equivalent.
Intended for those who are acquiring fundamental skills in reading, writing and mathematics and establishing a solid foundation for learning.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:Primary
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 1 – Primary education.

Values.Description: Intended for those attending professional programs or equivalent, such as law or medicine.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:ProfessionalLevel
dct:description: Other levels can typically be paired with Professional Level to refine a description of a level.

Values.Description: Intended for those who are under-prepared for learning at a particular level.
Intended for those attending secondary (high-school) level programs.
Intended for those who are enrolled in a degree program or other formal program at or below the baccalaureate, such as an associate’s degree, vocational, or technical program.
Intended for those in the second half of an undergraduate level program.
Intended for those at the later stages of secondary education, preparing for tertiary education or employment.
Values.Notes:
concept: audLevel:UpperSecondary
broader: audLevel:SecondaryLevel
dct:description: Aligns to ISCED 2011 level 3 – Upper secondary education.
